caveats: Suspicion echo is an UPPER BOUND, not an attribution: the deleted features encode clinician ordering behaviour and genuine information (a recently measured channel is also fresher data), so the drop bounds the suspicion component from above.
A low within-patient score is not automatically a flaw — a model may be honestly aimed at triage. It is a flaw only when the system is sold as early warning.
No clock-amplification measure is reported. That claim was attacked and failed: the headline was definitionally true, and only ~11% of the pairs pooled AUROC averages over are within-patient.
Pooled within-patient AUROC and the strictly per-stay version disagree by construction (Simpson's paradox). The stratified one is the honest answer.
verdict: selects patients at 0.796 and times the event at 0.653; lead time is -2.5h against its random null (no early-warning excess); loses 0.007 AUROC when measurement-pattern features are removed
